radiology_report:
Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis | 's-Hertogenbosch | 05 Jan 2025 | mpMRI Prostate

Clinical indication: A 72-year-old gentleman with a documented PSA value: 6.9 ng/mL and a historically positive biopsy bucket requires reassessment.

FINDINGS: The gland occupies 57.11 mL of space. Asymmetrical enlargement characterizes the organ. T2-weighted sequences isolate a 12 x 9 mm hypointense focus within the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Restricted diffusion appears on the DWI/ADC maps (b-value 1400) alongside low ADC signal, classifying this finding as PI-RADS: 4. Early focal enhancement emerges on the dynamic contrast phases. Examination confirms absent extraprostatic extension, negative seminal vesicle invasion, and lacking suspicious lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS: 4 lesion, right mid-gland peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 x 9 mm. With a prostate volume: 57.11 mL, the calculated PSA density: 0.121 ng/mL/mL. The csPCa predicted probability csPCa probability: 0.8325768.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial screening yielded a PSA reading of 3.5 ng/mL. Because of his age and the borderline nature of that value, a repeat assay was arranged together with a general health review. He noted mild hesitancy during urination but ruled out acute obstruction or haematuria. A six-month interval was established to track the trajectory.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Subsequent testing demonstrated a PSA rise to 4.1 ng/mL, which triggered a urology referral. A transrectal ultrasound-guided sampling confirmed low-volume adenocarcinoma. He remained on standard observation with periodic PSA checks and imaging. Latest labs record a PSA of 6.9 ng/mL, which necessitates this current appointment.
